title: How a Microwave Actually Heats Food

sections.name: Hook
lines: m_hook
Your microwave doesn't heat your food with heat. It shakes the water inside it.
m_title
Here's what's happening behind that door, in five steps.

sections.name: The magnetron
lines: m_magnetron
Step one. Inside is a device called a magnetron. It turns electricity into radio waves, called microwaves.
m_guide
A metal channel guides them into the box, where they bounce around off the metal walls.

sections.name: Shaking water
lines: m_water
Step two. Water molecules are lopsided. Slightly positive at one end, and negative at the other.
m_flip
The microwaves' electric field flips direction billions of times a second, and the water molecules keep twisting to follow it.
m_heat
All that twisting and jostling is heat. The food cooks itself, from the water inside.

sections.name: Hot and cold spots
lines: m_spots
Step three. The bouncing waves stack up into hot spots and cold spots inside the box.
m_turn
That's why the plate turns. It carries your food through the hot spots, so it cooks more evenly.

sections.name: Outside in
lines: m_depth
Step four. Microwaves only reach a few centimetres into food. The middle heats up more slowly, as the warmth spreads inward.
m_stir
That's why the instructions say stir halfway, or let it stand for a minute.
m_ice
Ice is tricky too. Its molecules are locked in place, so defrost mode pulses the power on and off, giving the heat time to spread.

sections.name: The door and the fork
lines: m_door
Step five. The door has a metal mesh with tiny holes. Light can get out, but the microwaves are too big to fit through.
m_fork
And metal with sharp edges, like a fork, can gather so much charge that it sparks. So keep it out.

sections.name: Recap
lines: w_recap
A magnetron makes the waves. The waves twist the water. The twisting makes heat. The plate spins to even it out, and the door keeps it all inside.
outro
Next time you wait for that beep, picture all those spinning water molecules. Follow for more of the tech you use every day.
